title: Autonomous batching policy evaluation and canary guardrails for cost-feedback recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Validate an autonomous recommendation engine that proposes batching and prefix/KV cache configurations for customer workloads, and implement canary guardrails that safely apply and revert config changes automatically. This ticket covers experiment design, instrumentation, dashboarding, and rollout/rollback automation for production safe A/B testing of config recommendations. Success criteria: (1) statistically significant cost reduction per workload cohort without >1% degradation in primary quality SLI, (2) zero-severity incidents from automatic config applies during canary windows, (3) monitoring and runbook for rollback are live in Console.
experiment_plan: A/B framework: split traffic at route level by cookie/key into Control (current config) and Treatment (autonomous recommended config). Run for 14 days per cohort with nightly power analysis. Primary metric: cost_per_1M_output_tokens_usd (decrease). Guardrail primary quality SLI: model_output_quality_delta on curated eval prompts must remain >= -0.5% relative to control. Secondary metrics: p95 latency, error_rate_5m, cache_hit_rate_prefix_kv. Cohorts: low-latency-sensitive (mobile-chat), high-throughput (batch-embeddings), long-context (chat-history). Minimum sample sizes computed per cohort; early-stopping rules if guardrails trip. Use stratified sampling to preserve clients with reserved capacity. A/B assignment implemented in traffic router (feature flag).
rollout_plan: Canary apply schedule: 1) Internal shadow run for 48h (no apply). 2) 1% traffic apply (24h) monitored by automated checks. 3) 5% traffic apply (48h) with human-in-loop approval. 4) 25% (48h) then 50% (24h) then 100% if all rollup checks pass. Automation will create a rollback ticket and trigger reversal if any automated guardrail trips. All applies via rollout API with audit log and dry-run available.
rollback_criteria: >=0.5 percentage point absolute increase in error_rate_5m sustained for 5 minutes
>=10% relative increase in p95_generation_latency_ms over baseline sustained for 15 minutes
model_output_quality_delta < -0.5% on eval_prompt_set_A aggregated over 2 hours
customer complaints flagged by support channel matching experiment cohorts
analysis_notes: Early signal from shadow run: recommended batch size + prefix caching reduced tokens_per_second cost by ~12% on embeddings workload without measurable quality delta.
Long-tail latency regressed for ~0.2% of requests when aggressive batching combined with KV prefetch; lowered prefetch depth fixed regression in staging.

Trade-off: larger batch sizes improve GPU utilization but increase queue_time_ms for latency-sensitive requests. Plan to use route-level policy to exclude latency-sensitive routes from aggressive knobs.
Quantization + batching combos were tested; INT8 path gave additional 6% token cost saving but requires separate kernel selection logic — scoped to next rhythm after runtime-1.22 stabilization.
Need to add provenance metadata to each applied config for auditing: who/why/experiment-id/diff.
